lp.heroLead: AI MedSmarter connects patients, pharmacists, physicians and pharmacies around one clear medication plan, with an assistant that always shows its sources.
lp.proto: Prototype · fictional data · not for clinical use
lp.sampleQuestion: What should I do if I miss a dose?
lp.sampleAnswer: Take it when you remember, unless the next dose is close. Never take a double dose. (Fictional demo answer.)
lp.problemTitle: Medicine plans are easy to lose track of
lp.problemNote: These are design hypotheses to validate with user research.
lp.problem1Body: Complex schedules and busy days lead to missed or doubled doses.
lp.problem2Body: Patients search the web and find unreliable, unsourced advice.
lp.problem3Body: Between visits, clinicians see little of adherence and side effects.
lp.solutionTitle: One plan, one assistant, one care team
lp.sol1Body: Schedules, reminders and warnings in plain language.
lp.sol2Body: Every answer cites approved sources and states how well they match.
lp.sol3Body: Pharmacists and physicians review what matters.
lp.howTitle: From prescription to peace of mind
lp.step1Body: From your physician or entered by you.
lp.step3Body: Log how you feel and ask the assistant.
lp.step4Body: Only what you choose to share.
lp.role.patient.1: Next dose and reminders at a glance
lp.role.pharmacy.1: Inventory and expiry in one view
lp.aiTitle: An assistant that shows its work
lp.aiLead: Not a generic chatbot. It answers from approved sources, tells you how well they match, and hands off to a person when it should.
lp.ai1: Source citations and evidence on every answer
lp.ai3: Says «I don't know» instead of guessing
lp.ai4: One tap to ask a pharmacist
lp.safetyTitle: AI advises. Rules and people decide.
lp.safe1Body: Interactions and contraindications come from a rules engine, never from a language model.
lp.safe2Body: Pharmacists and physicians confirm anything that affects treatment.
lp.safe3Body: Answers cite versioned, reviewed sources. No source, no answer.

sf.title: Medication safety check
sf.sub: A fixed set of written rules compares the medicines and records you entered. It is a check of your records, not medical advice.
sf.pro.title: Medication safety check for this patient
sf.pro.sub: Only what the care relationship and the patient's consent allow is used. Anything withheld is shown as not available, never as empty.
sf.intro: The check runs only when you ask for it. It does not run by itself in the background.
sf.none.title: No check has been run yet
sf.none.body: Run the check to see what the current rules can and cannot say about your records.
sf.history.title: Earlier checks
sf.err.notConnected.title: Not connected
sf.err.notConnected.body: This check needs a connection to the server. In-browser demo accounts cannot run it.
sf.err.blocked.title: This is not available to you
sf.err.blocked.body: Your account, your role or the patient's consent does not allow this check. Nothing was run.
sf.err.rate.title: Too many requests
sf.err.rate.body: Please wait a moment and try again.
sf.err.invalid.title: The check could not be started
sf.err.invalid.body: Some records are not in a form the check can use. Try again later.
sf.err.unavailable.title: The check is unavailable right now
sf.err.unavailable.body: A technical problem stopped it, so there is no result. This does not mean nothing was found. Please try again later.
sf.fa.unreviewed.title: Persian wording not yet reviewed
sf.fa.unreviewed.body: The Persian clinical wording on this page has not been reviewed by a clinician or a medical translator yet.
sf.status.CompletedWithFindings: The check found something to look at
sf.status.NoApprovedCoverage: No approved rules are in force
sf.status.Failed: The check could not be completed reliably
sf.statusBody.CompletedWithFindings: One or more rules matched your records. Each item below says what was matched, on what basis, and what a sensible next step is.
sf.statusBody.CompletedNoMatches: The rules that are in force found no match in the records they could read. That is not the same as being safe: see what the rules cover and what they do not.
sf.statusBody.Incomplete: Some information was missing, out of date, or could not be read, so some checks could not be done. Missing information is never treated as nothing found.
sf.statusBody.NoApprovedCoverage: No safety rule has been approved by two people yet, so nothing was checked against approved knowledge. Anything shown below comes from demonstration rules only.
sf.statusBody.Failed: An internal safety check failed. Do not rely on this result. Anything listed was kept so it is not lost.
sf.demo.finding: This comes from a demonstration rule or demonstration data. It is not approved advice.
sf.outdated.title: This result may be out of date
sf.outdated.body: Something changed after it was calculated. Nothing re-runs by itself; run the check again to refresh it.
sf.outdated.rules_changed: The set of rules in force changed.
sf.outdated.freshness_unknown: We could not tell whether anything changed.
sf.notSafety: A result without findings is not a statement that anything is safe.
sf.failed.title: Do not rely on this result
sf.failed.body: An internal consistency check failed. Please run it again, and talk to a pharmacist or physician about your medicines as you normally would.
sf.findings.title: What was found
sf.findings.sub: From rules that are approved and in force.
sf.demoFindings.title: Demonstration findings
sf.demoFindings.sub: Shown only to demonstrate how the check works. They are not advice.
sf.otherFindings.title: Notes that are not actionable
sf.otherFindings.sub: Based on information that is not fully validated.
sf.nothing.title: Nothing to show
sf.nothing.noCoverage: There is no approved rule, so there is nothing to report.
sf.nothing.incomplete: Nothing could be reported because information was missing or could not be read.

sf.why.Interaction: The medication reference lists these two together. Whether it matters for you depends on things this check does not look at, such as dose and timing.
sf.why.AllergyConflict: An allergy you recorded is linked to the same medicine, or to one with a shared ingredient, as a medicine you take.
sf.why.DuplicateIngredient: Two of your medicines contain the same ingredient according to the reference.
sf.why.DataQuality: The medicine is not in the reference (or its details are incomplete), so the other checks could not include it.
sf.why.ReportedSymptom: You rated a recorded symptom as strong and have not marked it as resolved. The check does not look for a cause.
